profile.campus: PLAY Katowice Gospodarcza Data Center Campus (DC1/DC2/DC3)
profile.address: Katowice Gospodarcza complex, ul. Gospodarcza, Katowice, Poland
profile.reading: This is PLAY Centrum Danych DC1, one of two existing data center buildings in the PLAY Katowice Gospodarcza complex in southern Poland, operated under the 3S Data Center brand. 3S Data Center belongs to the 3S Group, which Polish mobile operator Play, legally P4 sp. z o.o., acquired in 2019 for 410 million zloty, bringing the groups Katowice, Bytom, and other Polish data center sites under Play ownership. Trade press coverage describes DC1 and DC2 together occupying roughly 2,200 square meters within the Katowice Gospodarcza complex, which Play has since expanded with a newly built DC3 building of about 2,200 square meters more, bringing the complexs total footprint toward 4,400 square meters and adding Tier 3+ rated capacity. A separate directory listing places a PLAY branded Katowice facility at Ligocka 103, distinct from the Gospodarcza address cited in trade press for DC1 and DC2, a discrepancy this entry could not resolve with the sources available this session; this entry treats the Katowice Gospodarcza complex description from trade press as the more specific and recent source for this pair of buildings. Play also operates PLAY branded data centers elsewhere in Poland, including a facility in Bytom. Play itself was founded in February 2007 and grew into Polands second largest mobile network operator behind Orange Polska, reporting over 15.6 million subscribers by 2021. French telecom group Iliad agreed to buy Play in a 2.2 billion euro deal announced in September 2020, completing a tender offer that left Iliad holding 96.66 percent of Play by November 2020, and Iliad later merged UPC Poland, acquired separately from Liberty Global, into Play in August 2023, consolidating both mobile and fixed line infrastructure, including data center assets like this one, under the same French parent.
profile.research_note: Researched fresh 2026-09-04. This row was not previously scope-flagged but had never been researched. A conflicting directory listing gives one Katowice PLAY facility an address of Ligocka 103 rather than Gospodarcza, which this entry could not reconcile with trade press describing DC1 and DC2 as both sited in the Katowice Gospodarcza complex. The 2,200 sqm figure for DC1+DC2 combined is described in prose only, not applied as a fact-box technical_space_sqft value, since no per-building breakdown was found and applying the combined figure to each building individually would overstate size; facility_codes (DC1) used instead as the third fact-box key.

reading.body:
PLAY Centrum Danych DC1 is one of three data center buildings in the Katowice Gospodarcza complex in southern Poland, part of a telecom operator's infrastructure consolidation under French ownership.

The facility belongs to 3S Data Center, which Polish mobile operator Play acquired in 2019. Play itself became a subsidiary of French telecom group Iliad in 2020, and Iliad later merged additional Polish telecom assets into Play in 2023, centralizing mobile, fixed line, and data center operations under single ownership. This pattern reflects how telecom operators with existing real estate and power connections are becoming data center operators as compute demand grows.

DC1 and DC2 together occupy roughly 2,200 square meters within the complex, with a newer DC3 building adding another 2,200 square meters at Tier 3+ capacity. The data does not reveal power consumption, cooling infrastructure, or grid connection details for this facility. It also does not specify what workloads run there or whether any capacity is reserved for AI applications specifically. The precise boundary between DC1 and DC2 is unclear from available sources, and one directory listing places a PLAY facility at a different Katowice address, leaving some ambiguity about the exact footprint.

This facility sits in Katowice, an industrial city in Poland's energy-dense Silesia region. For the grid and compute constraint thesis, the relevance depends on whether this operator's data center expansion correlates with Polish power availability and whether Iliad's consolidation of telecom infrastructure is opening these facilities to higher-compute workloads. The data does not address either question.
